items.abstract: <jats:p>Large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate functionally correct code, but their ability to optimize the performance of complex, real-world software remains unclear. Existing evaluations primarily use self-contained algorithmic tasks harvested from online coding competitions, leaving the relevance of their results to practical software performance engineering (SPE) uncertain. Our study makes two contributions. First, we introduce PerfOpt, a reusable dataset of 65 real-world Java performance-optimization tasks, each with a human-authored solution, project context, tests, and Java Microbenchmark Harness (JMH) microbenchmarks. In contrast to existing LLM performance benchmarks, our focus in PerfOpt is on challenging, real-world optimization problems originating from software development practice rather than coding competitions. Second, we use PerfOpt as well as a sample drawn from an existing state-of-the-art algorithmic benchmark (EffiBench-X) to assess four commercial and open-weight LLMs under four prompting conditions, comparing plausible performance-focused solutions with the original code and human-authored baselines. We show that LLMs appear substantially stronger on EffiBench-X, generating plausible solutions for over 90\% of tasks, compared to around 60% of tasks in PerfOpt. More importantly, across all tasks, their median speedups on EffiBench-X are 2.1--2.8x, whereas they remain around 1.0x in PerfOpt. We conclude that existing benchmarks such as EffiBench-X draw an overly optimistic picture of current LLM capabilities for real-world SPE. In a real-world benchmark, existing LLMs struggle to both, identify important performance issues and to propose human-competitive fixes. More benchmarks such as PerfOpt are required as a reusable basis for evaluating future tool-supported SPE.</jats:p>
title: Beyond Algorithmic Tasks: Do Benchmarks Overestimate LLM Capability for Real-World Performance Optimization?
CentaurBench: Benchmarking LLM Capabilities on Augmenting vs. Automating Real-World Work Tasks
